content.title: About
content.content: Cantaloupe is a variety of sweet melon (Cucumis melo var. cantalupensis) grown in warm regions worldwide. Raw cantaloupe has orange‑red flesh, a sweet aroma, and a juicy texture. It is eaten fresh, added to salads, smoothies, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cantaloupe originates from the Mediterranean but is now cultivated in the USA, China, Turkey and many other countries.
In ancient Rome it was called “honey melon” because of its sweet flavor.
The seeds are edible but are usually removed before consumption.
Its water content reaches up to 90 %, making it an excellent refreshing fruit in hot weather.
Cantaloupe is rich in carotenoids, which give the flesh its orange color.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Because of its high water content, cantaloupe fits well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to melons.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improper handling can leave pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The natural sugars may be a concern for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat cantaloupe fresh, cut into cubes or wedges. Add it to fruit salads, smoothies, yogurts, and dessert sauces. The flesh can also be frozen for homemade ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole melons at room temperature for up to 5 days. Once cut, place in an airtight container and keep in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Frozen flesh can be kept in the freezer for up to 6 months.
